g1.label: 1. Cycling at night is ___ more dangerous than cycling in the day.
g1.why: Far + comparative strengthens the difference: far more dangerous.

g2.label: 2. The exam was not nearly ___ hard as we feared.
g2.why: Not nearly as … as: the adjective keeps its basic form.

g3.label: 3. This is the ___ expensive of the three phones.
g3.why: The least + adjective is the lowest of three.

g4.label: 4. The city is ___ big to explore in a single weekend.
g4.why: Too + adjective + to-infinitive: too big to explore.

g5.label: 5. Is the flat quiet ___ to study in?
g5.why: Enough follows the adjective: quiet enough.

g6.label: 6. The more you practise, ___ you will become.
g6.why: The more …, the more + adjective: the more fluent.

g7.label: 7. It was ___ a good offer that we accepted immediately.
g7.why: Such + a + adjective + noun: such a good offer.

g8.label: 8. Rents have risen twice ___ fast as salaries.
g8.why: Twice as + adjective + as shows a multiple.

g9.label: 9. There was ___ little time to answer all the questions.
g9.why: Too little: too goes before little, an uncountable amount.

g10.label: 10. She is ___ the most experienced person in the team.
g10.why: By far the + superlative: by far the most experienced.

g11.label: 11. At eight o’clock last night I ___ when my flatmate came home.
g11.why: The cooking was in progress when the flatmate came: past continuous.

g12.label: 12. I would be grateful ___ you could confirm the date.
g12.why: I would be grateful if you could… is a polite request.
